clue.text: Sporting shorter sweater, you say, as the wife may do

indicators.note: sporting can mean playing about or frolicking, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged
you say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt, giving the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone in a cropped jumper is compared with a domineering wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' looks like 'wearing', but it tells you to rearrange SHORTER, SWEATER and U (the letter that 'you, you say' sounds like).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a wife who is the dominant partner and makes the decisions at home.

clue.text: Father had potato cooked immediately

indicators.note: cooked suggests something altered or fiddled, so the letters of the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad has eaten a potato that someone prepared for him.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means without hesitation or delay, as quickly as a hat could be dropped as a starting signal.

clue.text: Ex-foreign secretary outside phone box

indicators.note: outside says the box word goes around the phone word

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard box
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: A former government minister stands beside a telephone kiosk.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'phone box' looks like one thing, the old red kiosk, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Carrington was Britain's Foreign Secretary under Margaret Thatcher from 1979 to 1982.

clue.text: Fruit for child-bearing mothers

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the mothers word holds the child word inside it

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A fruit is recommended for pregnant women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child-bearing' reads as pregnancy, which suits the surface about mothers; cryptically 'bearing' means carrying, a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsons are small dark purple plums.

clue.text: Item of clothing found at start of Rotten Row

parts.note: a tie is a piece of clothing worn round the neck

indicators.note: at the start of picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A garment is discovered at the beginning of a famous riding track.
explanation.walkthrough: ROTTEN ROW is a riding track in London's Hyde Park, which makes 'Row' look part of a name rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, as of seats rising one above another.

clue.text: Injured sister OK? No? Nephews, except Gilbert, remain calm

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters that follow are knocked into a new order
except means leaving out, so the Gilbert letters are taken from the nephews word

parts.note: W S Gilbert was the librettist of Gilbert and Sullivan

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a hurt sister is all right while telling the nephews to stay calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except' takes WS from NEPHEWS to leave NEPHE, and 'Injured' rearranges SISTER, OK, NO and NEPHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stay patient and not lose your temper.

clue.text: Father often bops around — it's become very tedious

indicators.note: around suggests moving about, so the letters of the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad keeps dancing about, which has become dreadfully boring.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means bored someone greatly, past tense, matching the sense of something that has proved deeply dull.

clue.text: Facts used in trial, stated at outset

indicators.note: out-set reads as set out or set differently, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Evidence given at a court hearing is presented at its beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outset' looks like 'start', but read as set out it tells you to rearrange STATED AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Test data is the set of figures fed into a trial run to check that something works.

clue.text: General attire: tonight's showing

indicators.note: showing means on display, so the answer can be seen inside the words before it

explanation.surface: An ordinary outfit will be on view this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an adjective about the attire, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Ireton was a Parliamentarian general in the English Civil War and Cromwell's son-in-law.

clue.text: One quivered as ex-convict produced spanner

definitions.meaning: one equipped with a quiver, the case that holds arrows
Jeffrey ..., the novelist, was jailed for perjury
read as ..., one that arches, so something that spans a gap

explanation.surface: A former prisoner trembled while handing over a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quivered' suggests trembling, but means 'carrying a quiver'; 'spanner' is not the tool but something that spans.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer carries a quiver; the novelist Jeffrey Archer served a prison sentence; an arch spans.

clue.text: Removed dress — good one, torn

parts.note: a saint is a good person, abbreviated ST
ripped means torn

explanation.surface: A fine garment was taken off after it got torn.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to take off clothing, so someone who has taken off their dress has stripped.

clue.text: I'm punched out in Africa

definitions.meaning: a small piece of paper punched from a card or ballot
a landlocked country in central Africa

explanation.surface: Someone says they are worn out somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Chads became famous in the disputed Florida vote count of the 2000 US presidential election.
explanation.definitionFit: A chad is the scrap punched out of a ballot card, and Chad is an African nation.

clue.text: Time spent with child

parts.note: sounds like hours of parenting, but means the length of a human pregnancy

explanation.definitionFit: A human pregnancy lasts about three quarters of a year, the time a woman is with child.

clue.text: Mother sees runt struggling for full development

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: struggling suggests something in disarray, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mother animal watches the weakest of her litter battling on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fully grown or developed is the state of maturity.

clue.text: When one's innings really gets going? A time to double score

definitions.text: When one's innings really gets going?
definitions.meaning: life is said to begin at this age, an innings being cricket's term for a turn batting, here a lifetime
a score is twenty, and twice twenty is the age meant

explanation.surface: A batsman's innings takes off at a moment when he doubles his runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings is a batter's turn; here it stands for a life, which the saying has beginning at this age.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying goes that life begins at this age, and the age is twice a score.

clue.text: Pa's hat's new in town

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad's hat is brand new and he's in town.
explanation.definitionFit: St Asaph is a small cathedral city in north Wales.

clue.text: Cavort wildly around East Ham

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters go about the next piece
wildly says the letters of the word before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone dances riotously round a district of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' turns CAVORT into OVRACT, and 'around' puts it about E. EAST HAM is a district of London, so 'Ham' looks part of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical way.

clue.text: Little number put on by the Queen just after quarter to five, before it's too late?

indicators.note: just after puts the Queen's letters straight after the others

parts.note: NO is the short form of number
clothes put on are worn
E, east, is one quarter of the compass
V is the Roman numeral five
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A short song is performed for the monarch at a quarter to five, ahead of a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter to five' reads as a time, but gives E (a compass point) next to V.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said of a chance that must be taken at once or lost, so before it is too late.

clue.text: You'd get cross from start to finish of this form of yarn

indicators.note: from start to finish says the first letter is moved to the end to make the cross word

parts.note: an ankh is the looped Egyptian cross

explanation.surface: Someone works out a cross-stitch pattern using a skein of wool.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: moving the first letter H of the answer to the end gives ANKH. Here the wordplay restores the H to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A hank is a coil or skein in which yarn is sold.

clue.text: Jersey occupier is one I sling mud at

parts.note: to slander is to sling mud at someone

explanation.surface: A resident of a Channel Island is the person I insult.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, not the sweater; ISLANDER read as I SLANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living on Jersey, a Channel Island, is an island dweller.

clue.text: Pop round by rail?

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Dad pops over by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by rail' looks like train travel, but the question mark points to a dado rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado rail is a moulding fixed along a wall, so the word describes this kind of rail.

clue.text: Nobel prizewinner coming from Tyneside to Fleet Street

parts.note: Tyneside is in north-east England, NE
the Royal Navy, RN, is Britain's fleet

explanation.surface: A Nobel laureate travels from Newcastle to London's newspaper district.
explanation.walkthrough: FLEET STREET was London's newspaper district, but 'Fleet' and 'Street' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Walther Nernst won the 1920 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his work in thermochemistry.

clue.text: Make a mistake with message

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
and means together with

explanation.surface: Someone gets a message wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand originally meant a message carried for someone, the older sense of the word.

clue.text: These may be given away by accountants to the rich and well-dressed

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant, so CAS for several
toffs are rich, smartly dressed people

explanation.surface: Accountants hand over items to wealthy, elegant people.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-off clothes are ones discarded by their owners, often given to others or to charity.
